A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Control work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison. The original system-identification appendix moves from Appendix E to Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original elastic-strip simulations, optimizer comparisons with numerical losses and runtimes, real-robot demonstrations, and an experimentally identified material parameter.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds iCEM evaluations and a learned implicit-model experiment using collected slinky force–strain measurements.

M1.justification: The specified backward procedure changes: v2 removes the additional terminal S^T a term and separate running-loss sensitivity term from the z-adjoint, consistently revising Sections 3.1–3.2, Appendix A, and Algorithm 1. Appendix B also changes the bending-energy sum to include node i=1. These alter the documented gradient computation and equilibrium model; implementation changes or experimental reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds experimental slinky force–strain data and sinusoidal strain tracking through a learned equilibrium model. This is a limited extension beyond the retained simulated and physical elastic-strip tasks. Triangular reference trajectories already appear in v1.

E2.justification: iCEM is newly evaluated across all three principal tasks and becomes a primary comparator in Table 1 and Figure 4. SPSA and Adjoint-only remain. CEM's numerical comparisons are retained in Appendix E, Table 2, so the central comparator set expands rather than simply replacing CEM.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes the stated SPSA estimator from averaging two perturbation pairs per update to using one, resolving its inconsistency with v1's main-text account of two evaluations. The new learned-model experiment introduces a train-then-freeze protocol before control optimization. Existing DLO metrics, horizons, and update budgets remain; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a small applicability case study asking whether the sensitivity pipeline works through a learned equilibrium residual, reporting force–strain fitting and successful strain tracking. The existing RHC-removal ablation and DLO manipulation demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report table results as mean ± standard deviation and Figure 4 curves as mean ± one standard error over four cases. Added comparator results follow the existing practice. No changes to evaluation-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds iCEM results and convergence curves for all three tasks, including Task 3 runtime 9907.3 seconds and best loss 1.2×10^-2, plus learned-model tracking losses around 10^-8–10^-11. Original SPSA, CEM, and adjoint table values are retained across Tables 1–2. The identified value 0.0514 is retained with its unit corrected from inverse metres to metres.

T1.justification: Beyond the revised adjoint equations, Appendix C replaces the Cε guarantee based on a bounded tangent derivative with a fixed-segment CηS bound using within-step tangent variation, claiming O(Δλ) consistency under Lipschitz continuity. It adds a proof and explicit boundedness assumptions. Appendix B also replaces the global argmin characterization with solver-selected local stationarity.

C1.justification: The central proxy-adjoint and RHC contributions remain. v2 foregrounds sequential implicit optimization and adds demonstrated applicability to learned equilibrium models. Its conclusion replaces the 19–127× SPSA/CEM speedup and 3–6-order loss claim with up to 195× against SPSA/iCEM and a less specific lower-loss claim.

C2.justification: The discussion adds specific qualifications concerning learned-model quality, omitted fast dynamics, friction, damping, contact, and scaling to 2D/3D bodies. It clarifies that RHC does not remove underlying ill-conditioning. Branch-locality and bifurcation limitations already existed, while v1's explicit limited-lookahead caveat is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-page access instructions for code, videos, and results; iCEM-specific reuse and correlation settings; and clearer quadrature and Jacobian-caching details. Most original implementation information remains. However, smoothing and variance settings previously documented for CEM are no longer explicitly assigned to that retained baseline.

R1.justification: v2 adds Agrawal et al. on differentiable convex optimization layers and Tong et al.'s DDG survey, while removing Liang et al. and Look et al. The distinction from single fixed-point/KKT methods is emphasized but already present in v1. Pinneri et al. was already cited; iCEM's evaluation is new.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodological explanations, discussion, and substantial appendix passages are rewritten and expanded. The appendices are reorganized around additional baseline and learned-model sections, and acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. This is extensive editorial revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The entire appendix changes from two-column to single-column layout, substantially redisplaying equations, Algorithm 1, and Figure 6. Figure 4 is redrawn with iCEM curves and legends, Table 1's presentation and caption are revised, and Table 2 redisplays retained CEM comparisons. The principal task illustrations remain.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the internal consistency of the written proxy-adjoint recursion, clarifies assumptions and runtime accounting, and adds iCEM comparisons while preserving CEM evidence. The learned-model extension is only briefly substantiated without plots or training specifications in the PDF, and some CEM implementation detail is lost. These tradeoffs support a limited net quality improvement.
